description:
## Problem
After the rework only DuckDB can run TPC-DI. Databricks ran the old TPC-DI.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- 2026-11-20: "SQL on DuckDB first, proven with the audit; then the other SQL platforms ... one PR each" and, for platforms without published results, "Plan a pull request for every one of them."
- 2026-11-21, platforms that cannot run the official audit as written: "Modify the audit per platform; each change needs my approval." Flow: "Each platform step lists its proposed changes and stops for my approval before its pull request is armed. Changes are recorded in the result."
- 2026-11-21, platforms with no XML reader or extension: "Parse client-side in Python inside the timed phase; recorded in the result."
- 2026-11-21, Databricks-specific optimisations: "Optional tuning, off by default; the base SQL is the same on every platform."
- 2026-11-20: third-party engine extensions are allowed for XML.
- 2026-11-21, Databricks: "First cloud platform, after the milestone stop and your cost approval."

## Change
Add `sql_compat/rules/query_adapter/tpcdi_<platform>.py` for Databricks with the registered choices for the four per-platform points (file ingestion into staging, XML parsing, how history-tracked rows are applied, flag storage), the golden renders of the canonical SQL for this platform, the adapter's ingestion hook, the visibility session, and the platform on the allowed list. The ETL is the canonical DuckDB-dialect SQL rendered by the existing translation path; no per-platform SQL file. Where translation is not enough, a registered rule supplies the alternative statement and it is recorded in the result. Copying source files to a platform's stage before the run is untimed; reading them into staging is timed. Once this platform passes, its result may be published and its cell in the seed workflow re-enabled without asking, because the first DuckDB publication has been approved (owner, 2026-11-21: "After I approve the first DuckDB publication, later platforms publish and regain seed cells once they pass, without asking."). If this pass brings the number of platforms that pass the full audit, DuckDB included, to three, set the registry status to `beta` and update the site support-status row, with a test that counts the allowed list (owner: DuckDB counts as one of the three). Changelog fragment. The Databricks project's clustering, engine settings and partitioned staging are optional tuning, off by default. Also run the project's own Incremental workflow on the same DIGen data and compare warehouses with the harness; differences must be on the expected list. Tuning uses BenchBox's existing tuning configuration; no new switch (owner, 2026-11-21).

## Decision gates
First run Appendix A, B and C on Databricks with the specification's minor substitutions only. If any statement needs more, list each proposed change (statement, change, reason, and proof on a fixture that the changed and unchanged statements agree where both run), and stop for the owner's approval before arming; approved changes live in a registered rule, never in the shipped TPC file, and are recorded in the result under the audit block. The strategy for history-tracked rows is stated in the pull request and must keep committed rows visible during the update (Clause 4.3.5.8). If Databricks has no XML reader or extension, parse client-side in Python inside the timed phase and record it. Blocked until the owner approves a live run and a budget for this platform after the milestone report; no live cloud run otherwise.

## Verification rubric
Pass: through `make heavy-run` at scale 3, a Databricks run passes the full audit and produces a PASSED result with the label; substitutions, approved modifications, the four choices and any extension or client-side parsing are recorded in the result; the comparison harness against BenchBox's DuckDB warehouse built from the same staging manifest shows no row difference in any warehouse table (any difference is a finding, triaged before arming); a negative control fails the run; platforms not yet done still refuse; `make platform-manifest-check`, `make compat-inventory-check` and `make pr-preflight` pass. A run with no tuning option renders the same SQL as the canonical render for Databricks (test).

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name) the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner, and the pull request is not armed until the owner approves it. Test-only hook names are the implementer's choice and are listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21).
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run until the owner's budget approval for this platform is recorded on this item; then only within it. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row is shown to the owner and the pull request is not armed until the owner approves it.
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
